# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: X11 colour names in OSC 4 / 10 / 11 / 12 sets   (issue #187, wave 8)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/osc_color_names_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output, 2026-11-03; do not edit osc_color_spec.txt)
# Companion: osc_color_spec.txt (the colour-spec parser, sets, queries and resets; same table format and the same TEST THEME T / T2),
# rgb_names.txt (the 782-entry table, name TAB r TAB g TAB b), notes.md (the research answers).
#
# FORMAT  exactly osc_color_spec.txt (read by tests/osc_color.rs, which the implementer points at this file too): `### ID`, `size: RxC`,
#   `step: feed <bytes>` (\e = ESC, \x07 = BEL, \xNN, \u{H}, \t \r \n; `\x20` is a space), the generated step
#   `step: feed (OSC 11 ; then N bytes of 'a', then BEL)` (N may carry commas), `step: set theme T|T2`, `reply: <bytes>|none`,
#   `expect: fg|bg|cursor|pal[N]=#rrggbb ...`, `overrides: <keys>|none` (fg bg cursor pal[N] ascending), `gen: +1|same`
#   (relative to the previous `gen:` line), `screen:`/`cursor:`/`requests: []`, and `cite:` / `note:` / `flags:` (not checked).
#   Steps and checks interleave in fixture order, so one row can set several names in turn and check the colour after each.
#   Rows with no `reply:` line do not check replies; rows meant to be silent say `reply: none`.
#   Every row runs whole, byte by byte and split in two at every offset of every feed step (the generated 65,536-byte rows split only
#   at their 64 first and last offsets). The expected values never equal the theme default of the colour they set, so `gen: +1`
#   is meaningful; rows that repeat a value say `gen: same`.
#   TEST THEME T: fg #d0d0d0, bg #101010, cursor #ffcc00, palette[i] = (i, 255 - i, i XOR 0x55); T2: fg #aabbcc, bg #223344, cursor #00ff00.
#
# SOURCES (fetched 2026-11-03; the first five are PRIMARY)
#   [RGB]  X.org rgb.txt, https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/app/rgb (blob 7096643760e1a9bcb7887b9a8b6c17f75bf500f6, sha256 f8e3a7be...b6f0,
#          782 lines, last changed 2023-07-10 by 0d2caece; tag rgb-1.1.1). Licence: COPYING in that repo (MIT/X11 + Open Group notice):
#          the implementer's file header must carry it (saved next to this file as COPYING.xorg-rgb).
#   [XS]   X server https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver os/oscolor.c, OsLookupColor() (tag xorg-server-21.1.13 and main eae2c210):
#          binary search over the BuiltinColors[] table (782 entries, the same set as [RGB]), `strncasecmp(entry, name, len)` and
#          `len == strlen(entry)`: ASCII case-insensitive, whole-string, spaces significant. dix/dispatch.c ProcLookupColor calls it.
#   [XP]   libX11 https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libx11 src/ParseCol.c XParseColor(): `#` specs, then the Xcms path
#          (src/xcms/cmsColNm.c _XcmsResolveColorString: `rgb:`/`rgbi:`/CIE specs, then _XcmsLookupColorName which lowercases and
#          REMOVES SPACES but searches only the Xcms colour database, src/xcms/Xcms.txt: three entries "cms red/green/blue"), then
#          the LookupColor request to the server ([XS]). So a name resolves iff it is a [XS] entry (or one of the three cms names).
#   [XT]   xterm https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots (XTERM_PATCH 412, master as fetched 2026-11-03) misc.c: do_osc,
#          ChangeAnsiColorRequest (OSC 4), ChangeColorsRequest (OSC 10..12), AllocateAnsiColor, AllocateTermColor, xtermAllocColor
#          (the one call to XParseColor for a name, OSC 4 and 10..12 alike), xtermIsPrintable.
#   [CSS]  CSS Color Module Level 4, section "Named Colors": https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#named-colors (148 names, all in [RGB]).
#   [KT] [WZ] [GH] [AL]  comparison only: kitty gen/color_names.py + colors.c parse_color (lowercases AND trims blanks, 753 names,
#          X11 values); WezTerm color-types/src/lib.rs + rgb.txt (the same 782 lines, ASCII-lowercased exact match, X11 values, plus
#          transparent/none/clear); Ghostty src/terminal/x11_color.zig (res/rgb.txt, ASCII-case-insensitive exact match); Alacritty
#          takes no names for OSC colours (from memory, not re-fetched).
#
# DECISIONS (D-Nxx; the lead confirms; the rows follow the recommendation; D-NAMES of osc_color_spec.txt is superseded)
#   D-N1  MATCH RULE (confirmed by [XS]/[XP]/[XT], replaces the brief's "until confirmed" text): the name is compared as raw bytes,
#         ASCII case-insensitively, over its WHOLE length, against every entry of the 782-entry table, spaces significant. The table
#         has "dark slate gray" AND "DarkSlateGray", so both match (in any case: "DARKSLATEGRAY", "Dark Slate Gray"); "dark slategray",
#         "darkslate gray", "dark  slate gray" do not. Tessera must NOT strip spaces (xterm does not either: that is a client-side
#         Xcms step with a three-name database). The 106 spaced names all have a compact twin, so "strip spaces then lowercase" would
#         accept the same names PLUS misplaced-space forms; the exact rule is the xterm one.
#   D-N2  No trimming: a leading or trailing blank (0x20) makes an unknown name. (kitty trims; xterm does not.)
#   D-N3  Non-ASCII: the matcher works on bytes and folds only A-Z to a-z. Any byte >= 0x80 makes the name unknown (no Unicode folding:
#         U+212A KELVIN SIGN must not match "khaki"). Invalid UTF-8 is just such bytes.
#   D-N4  C0 controls (0x00-0x06, 0x08-0x17, 0x19, 0x1C-0x1F: TAB LF CR NUL included) never reach the terminal (tessera-vt drops them in an
#         OSC), so `red\x00` is `red`, `re\td` is `red`, `dark\tslate gray` is `darkslate gray` (unknown). DEL 0x7F stays and makes the
#         name unknown. Tessera and xterm may differ for NUL (unverified, flagged).
#   D-N5  TABLE: all 782 entries of the 2014+ rgb.txt, including the 10 CSS-4 additions (aqua crimson fuchsia indigo lime olive rebecca
#         purple silver teal) and the 20 "x11 ..."/"web ..." aliases (gray green maroon purple, each in spaced and compact, gray also
#         grey). Values are taken from the file (gray50 = 127, not computed). Count asserted in a test: 782. The name table the
#         X server ships today is this table (21.1.13 and main).
#   D-N6  LENGTH CAP: the longest entry is "light goldenrod yellow", 22 bytes. A name of 23+ bytes is rejected BEFORE the table
#         search by a constant (MAX_NAME_LEN = 22). xterm has no such cap (it drops only > 65535 bytes, xtermAllocColor), so this is
#         Tessera's own bound (S5); it never rejects a valid name.
#   D-N7  UNKNOWN NAME: OSC 10/11/12 chain: that colour is skipped, later pieces still apply (D-QUERY; xterm ChangeColorsRequest
#         ignores AllocateTermColor's result). OSC 4: processing stops at the failed pair, earlier pairs stay (D-STOP4; xterm
#         `code < 0 -> break`). No reply, no generation bump, no override, no trace of the name (S1, S8: log the length only).
#   D-N8  NOT ACCEPTED (ignored like any unknown name): CSS keywords (transparent, currentcolor, none, clear), xterm's
#         XtDefaultForeground / XtDefaultBackground (OSC 10..12 only in xterm), the Xcms "cms red/green/blue", and the spec
#         syntaxes rgbi:/CIE*/TekHVC (D-SPEC). A `?` is a query only as the WHOLE piece (OQ19), never part of a name.
#   D-N9  X11 WINS over CSS: gray/grey (190, not 128), green (0,255,0, not 0,128,0), maroon (176,48,96, not 128,0,0), purple (160,32,240,
#         not 128,0,128): exactly these five names differ between the 148 CSS names and rgb.txt. The CSS values stay reachable through
#         the "web gray/green/maroon/purple" aliases. (osc_color_spec.txt's header says WezTerm uses CSS names: wrong, see [WZ].)
#   D-N10 TERMINATORS: BEL, ST, and 8-bit ST (only in S8C1T mode) all end a name; 0x9C in 7-bit mode is payload and makes the name
#         unknown; CAN/SUB dispatch what was collected (ADR 0022 D-CAN; xterm aborts: xterm-quirk).
#
# MUTATION CHECKS (measured 2026-11-03 in a scratch copy of main with a linear-scan stand-in for the lookup over rgb_names.txt; the
#   failing rows named are those that failed; the scratch table was keyed by lowercase names)
#   names ignored (today)                  -> 49 rows fail (every row that sets a colour by name)
#   case-sensitive compare                 -> NA01 NA05 NA06 NB02 NC01 NC02 ND01 ND02 NE05 NE06 NF03 NG02 (every row with an upper-case letter)
#   CSS gray/grey/green/maroon/purple      -> NB06 NB09 NC02 NF01 NF02 NG05 NH03 NL02 (green and gray appear in several rows)
#   strip spaces before the lookup         -> ND03 NE04 NE07 NI02 NJ03
#   trim blanks around the name            -> ND03 NI02 NJ03
#   Unicode case folding (to_lowercase)    -> NC03 NJ05
#   length cap of 21                       -> ND01 NI01 (the longest entry is rejected); a cap above 22 is not observable in a row:
#                                             the flood test (1,000,000 names of 64 KiB, flat memory) and a unit test on the constant cover it
#   unknown name stops a 10/11/12 chain    -> NH03 ;  unknown name does not stop OSC 4 -> NH04 NG07
#   reply echoes the name                  -> NG02
#   whole fixture against the stand-in (all 70 rows, whole / bytewise / every 2-way split): passes.
# =============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NA. The documented examples (brief #187 "done")

### NA01_darkslategray_compact_st
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;DarkSlateGray\e\\
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
overrides: bg
gen: +1
reply: none
cite: [OSC] OSC 11 ; DarkSlateGray ST sets the background to rgb.txt DarkSlateGray = 47 79 79 = #2f4f4f (same as rgb:2f/4f/4f); D-N1; [XL] names come from rgb.txt
flags: control

### NA02_dark_slate_gray_spaced_st
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;dark slate gray\e\\
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
overrides: bg
gen: +1
cite: rgb.txt has the line "47 79 79 <TAB><TAB>dark slate gray"; the server compares the whole name, spaces included (OsLookupColor); D-N1
flags: control

### NA03_darkslategray_lower_bel
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;darkslategray\x07
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
overrides: bg
gen: +1
cite: case-insensitive match of the compact twin "DarkSlateGray" (strncasecmp, os/oscolor.c OsLookupColor); D-N1
flags: control

### NA04_osc4_red
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;red\x07
expect: pal[1]=#ff0000 pal[2]=#02fd57
overrides: pal[1]
gen: +1
reply: none
cite: [XT] ChangeAnsiColorRequest -> ChangeOneAnsiColor -> AllocateAnsiColor -> xtermAllocColor -> XParseColor: the same lookup as OSC 10..12; red = 255 0 0
flags: control

### NA05_gray50_grey50_resolve_per_rgb_txt
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;gray50;2;grey50;3;GRAY50\x07
expect: pal[1]=#7f7f7f pal[2]=#7f7f7f pal[3]=#7f7f7f
overrides: pal[1] pal[2] pal[3]
cite: rgb.txt "127 127 127 gray50" and "grey50": 127 = 0x7f (NOT 128: CSS has no gray50); D-N1, D-N5
flags: control

### NA06_old_OI_NAME_row_flipped
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;Red\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
gen: same
step: feed \e]11;light goldenrod\x07
expect: bg=#eedd82
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;gray50\x07
expect: bg=#7f7f7f
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;DarkSlateBlue\x07
expect: bg=#483d8b
gen: +1
overrides: bg
cite: the five names of OI-NAME_x11_names_are_ignored in osc_color_spec.txt (now OI-NAME_x11_names_are_accepted), which #187 flips to these results (ff0000, ff0000, eedd82, 7f7f7f, 483d8b); the second one sets the value already held, so no generation bump (D-GEN)
flags: control decision

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NC. Case: ASCII case-insensitive (the server uses strncasecmp)

### NC01_case_variants_of_darkslategray
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;DARKSLATEGRAY;2;DaRkSlAtEgRaY;3;DARK SLATE GRAY;4;Dark Slate Gray;5;darkSLATEgray\x07
expect: pal[1]=#2f4f4f pal[2]=#2f4f4f pal[3]=#2f4f4f pal[4]=#2f4f4f pal[5]=#2f4f4f
overrides: pal[1] pal[2] pal[3] pal[4] pal[5]
cite: [XS] os/oscolor.c OsLookupColor: strncasecmp(table name, input) with an exact length compare; OSC 4 stops at the first failure, so pairs 2..5 prove each variant
flags: control

### NC02_case_variants_via_osc11_each
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;RED\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
step: feed \e]11;Green\x07
expect: bg=#00ff00
step: feed \e]11;bLuE\x07
expect: bg=#0000ff
step: feed \e]11;YELLOW\x07
expect: bg=#ffff00
overrides: bg
cite: each name differs from the previous colour, so an unmatched case variant leaves the old value and the next expect fails
flags: control

### NC03_unicode_case_folding_is_not_ascii
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;\u{212a}haki\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{17f}now\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{130}vory\x07
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
reply: none
cite: D-N3: KELVIN SIGN U+212A lowercases to k in Unicode (a char::to_lowercase / eq_ignore_case would accept "Khaki"), LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S U+017F uppercases to S ("snow"); the match is ASCII-only bytes (eq_ignore_ascii_case); [XS] strncasecmp in the C locale
flags: negative security

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ ND. Spaces: significant, exactly the variants rgb.txt lists

### ND01_spaced_and_compact_twins
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;light goldenrod;2;LightGoldenrod;3;lightgoldenrod;4;light goldenrod yellow;5;LightGoldenrodYellow;6;lightgoldenrodyellow\x07
expect: pal[1]=#eedd82 pal[2]=#eedd82 pal[3]=#eedd82 pal[4]=#fafad2 pal[5]=#fafad2 pal[6]=#fafad2
overrides: pal[1] pal[2] pal[3] pal[4] pal[5] pal[6]
cite: rgb.txt lists both "light goldenrod" and "LightGoldenrod" (238 221 130) and both "light goldenrod yellow" and "LightGoldenrodYellow" (250 250 210); 6 pairs fit under the cut of 7
flags: control

### ND02_every_spaced_name_has_a_compact_twin_sample
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;navy blue;2;NavyBlue;3;navyblue;4;navy;5;medium spring green;6;mediumspringgreen\x07
expect: pal[1]=#000080 pal[2]=#000080 pal[3]=#000080 pal[4]=#000080 pal[5]=#00fa9a pal[6]=#00fa9a
overrides: pal[1] pal[2] pal[3] pal[4] pal[5] pal[6]
cite: all 106 spaced entries of rgb.txt have a compact twin (checked by scripts/cmp2.py); "navy blue" and "navy" are both entries (0 0 128)
flags: control

### ND03_misplaced_spaces_are_not_names
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;dark slategray\x07
step: feed \e]11;darkslate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark  slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark slate  gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark slate gray \x07
step: feed \e]11; dark slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;d ark slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark slate g ray\x07
step: feed \e]11;light goldenrodyellow\x07
step: feed \e]11;lightgoldenrod yellow\x07
step: feed \e]11;navy  blue\x07
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
reply: none
cite: D-N2: [XS] OsLookupColor compares the whole string with strncasecmp and `len == strlen(entry)`: spaces are significant and never stripped; the client-side Xcms lookup strips spaces and lowers case but its only database (libX11 src/xcms/Xcms.txt) holds "cms red/green/blue", so "darkslate gray" does NOT resolve in xterm. Only names rgb.txt lists resolve
flags: negative xterm-quirk decision

### ND04_other_whitespace_in_a_name
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;dark\x20slate\x20gray\x07
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;red\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
step: feed \e]11;dark\u{a0}slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark\u{2003}slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;dark\u{3000}slate gray\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
cite: D-N2/D-N3: only the ASCII space 0x20 is a blank in a name; NBSP, EM SPACE and IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE are non-ASCII bytes and never match; \x20 is the same byte as a space
flags: negative

### ND05_tab_lf_cr_are_removed_by_the_parser
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;dark \tslate gray\x07
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;re\nd\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;gr\rey50\x07
expect: bg=#7f7f7f
overrides: bg
cite: ADR 0022 facts / osc_spec.txt FACT 3: tessera-vt (vte) drops C0 0x00-0x06, 0x08-0x17, 0x19, 0x1C-0x1F inside an OSC, TAB LF CR NUL included, so the terminal sees "dark slate gray", "red", "grey50" (OZ06 precedent). xterm: unverified (a NUL would end its C string; the other C0 bytes are not printable and do_osc returns for numbers other than 0..2)
flags: decision xterm-quirk unverified

### NE05_gray_family_names

### NE06_numbered_variants_of_other_colours
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;red1;2;red4;3;AntiqueWhite1;4;antiquewhite4;5;DarkSlateGray1\x07

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NF. X11 versus CSS: X11 wins (lead decision D-X11)

### NF01_the_five_disagreements_are_x11
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;gray;2;grey;3;green;4;maroon;5;purple\x07

overrides: pal[1] pal[2] pal[3] pal[4] pal[5]
cite: rgb.txt: gray/grey 190 190 190, green 0 255 0, maroon 176 48 96, purple 160 32 240; CSS Color 4 named colors (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#named-colors) has gray/grey #808080, green #008000, maroon #800000, purple #800080. These five are the ONLY name-value differences between the 148 CSS names and rgb.txt (checked by script; every CSS name is also an rgb.txt entry)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NG. Queries with names: a ? is never a name, a reply never echoes a name

### NG01_query_form_still_queries
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\x07\e]11;?\e\\
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07\e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\e\\
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
cite: [XT] `!strcmp(thisName, "?")` is tested BEFORE the name lookup in ChangeColorsRequest and ChangeAnsiColorRequest
flags: control

### NG02_reply_after_a_name_set_is_rgb_not_the_name
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;dark slate gray\x07
step: feed \e]11;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:2f2f/4f4f/4f4f\x07
step: feed \e]4;1;gray50\x07\e]4;1;?\e\\
reply: \e]4;1;rgb:7f7f/7f7f/7f7f\e\\
step: feed \e]10;LightGoldenrodYellow\e\\\e]10;?\x07
reply: \e]10;rgb:fafa/fafa/d2d2\x07
cite: [XT] ReportColorRequest / ReportAnsiColorRequest print `rgb:%04x/%04x/%04x` of the stored value (8-bit * 257); the name is not kept for the reply. S1: no reply echoes the name
flags: control security

### NG03_query_then_set_by_name_in_one_chain

flags: control

### NG04_set_by_name_then_query_in_one_chain

### NG05_osc4_query_set_query_with_names

### NG06_question_mark_in_a_name_is_not_a_query

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NI. Length: the longest entry is 22 bytes; longer is rejected before lookup

cite: D-N6: "light goldenrod yellow" is 22 bytes, the longest rgb.txt name (next: LightGoldenrodYellow, 20); 250 250 210; MAX_NAME_LEN = 22

### NI02_over_the_cap_rejected
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;light goldenrod yellow \x07
step: feed \e]11;light goldenrod yellowx\x07
step: feed \e]11;light  goldenrod yellow\x07

reply: none
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
cite: D-N6: 23 bytes and more never match anything and are dropped before the table search (S5: the cap is a constant, no allocation sized by the name); the first four are near-misses of the longest entry, the last is `red` + 22 spaces
flags: negative security

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NJ. Trailing junk, blanks, NUL and non-ASCII

### NJ01_semicolon_ends_a_name_and_starts_the_next_colour
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red;\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: bg
cite: OS23: the empty piece after `red;` is the (empty) name of colour 12 and is skipped; `;` is a separator, never part of a name
flags: control

### NJ02_semicolon_splits_a_spaced_name
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;light;goldenrod\x07
expect: bg=#101010 cursor=#daa520
overrides: cursor
cite: the chain splits at `;`: "light" (unknown, skipped) goes to colour 11, "goldenrod" (218 165 32) sets colour 12; a name never contains `;`
flags: decision

### NJ03_trailing_junk_and_blanks
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red \x07
step: feed \e]11; red\x07
step: feed \e]11;red.\x07
step: feed \e]11;red,\x07
step: feed \e]11;red!\x07
step: feed \e]11;red#\x07
step: feed \e]11;red/\x07
step: feed \e]11;red:\x07
step: feed \e]11;red(\x07
step: feed \e]11;red1x\x07
step: feed \e]11;\x7fred\x07
step: feed \e]11;red\x7f\x07
step: feed \e]11;re\x7fd\x07
reply: none
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
cite: D-N2: no trimming (the server compares the whole string; kitty colors.c trim_view trims and would accept the blank forms: kitty differs); DEL 0x7f is not removed by the parser (osc_spec FACT 3) so it is part of the name
flags: negative

### NJ04_nul_and_c0_are_removed_by_the_parser
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red\x00\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;\x00dark slate gray\x07
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;gr\x01ey\x1f50\x07
expect: bg=#7f7f7f
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;dark slate\x00 gray\x07
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
gen: +1
overrides: bg
cite: D-N4: ADR 0022 facts (osc_spec.txt FACT 3, row OZ06 precedent): vte drops 0x00-0x06, 0x08-0x17, 0x19, 0x1C-0x1F inside an OSC before the terminal sees them, so the four names are red, "dark slate gray", "grey50", "dark slate gray". xterm may differ (unverified: its sos_table entry for NUL was not read; do_osc walks a C string, so a NUL would end the string: red, an empty name, "gr" or similar, "dark slate")
flags: decision xterm-quirk unverified

### NJ05_non_ascii_never_matches
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;r\u{e9}d\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{ff21}red\x07
step: feed \e]11;red\u{200b}\x07
step: feed \e]11;red\u{a0}\x07
step: feed \e]11;gr\u{e1}y\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{212a}haki\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{ff32}\u{ff25}\u{ff24}\x07
step: feed \e]11;\u{1f534}\x07
step: feed \e]11;red\u{301}\x07
reply: none
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
cite: D-N3: [XS] strncasecmp over bytes; no entry contains a byte >= 0x80, so any such byte makes the name unknown. libX11 _XcmsCopyISOLatin1Lowered folds Latin-1 (e.g. 0xC0 -> 0xE0) but only for the Xcms database, which has three "cms" names; nothing folds a UTF-8 sequence to ASCII
flags: negative security

### NJ06_invalid_utf8_bytes
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;\xffred\x07
step: feed \e]11;red\xff\x07
step: feed \e]11;re\xc0\xafd\x07
step: feed \e]11;gr\xe9y\x07
step: feed \e]11;\x80\x07
reply: none
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
cite: D-N3: raw bytes >= 0x80 pass through vte unchanged (osc_spec FACT 3) and never match (OZ05 precedent); the matcher works on bytes, not on str, so it cannot panic or lossily convert
flags: negative security

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ NK. Terminators: BEL, ST, 8-bit ST; names ending at a C1 byte

### NK01_bel_and_st_both_set

expect: bg=#ff0000
step: feed \e]11;blue\e\\
expect: bg=#0000ff
overrides: bg

### NK02_8bit_st_in_8bit_mode_sets
size: 24x80
step: feed \e G\x9d11;dark slate gray\x9c
expect: bg=#2f4f4f
overrides: bg
gen: +1
step: feed \x9d4;1;red\x9c
expect: pal[1]=#ff0000
reply: none
cite: #96 D1: after S8C1T (ESC SP G) 0x9D opens an OSC and 0x9C is ST (c1_spec.txt S05); a name ends at the 8-bit ST like at BEL
flags: control

### NK03_8bit_st_in_7bit_mode_is_payload
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red\x9c\x07
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
reply: none
step: feed \e]11;red\u{9c}\x07
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
reply: none
cite: #96 D1 / OQ26 / osc_spec FACT 5: raw 0x9C and U+009C do not terminate an OSC in 7-bit mode; they are part of the name "red\x9c", which is unknown; the BEL then ends the OSC. (xterm in UTF-8 mode ignores U+0080..U+009F in a string.)
flags: negative decision

### NK04_can_and_sub_dispatch_what_was_collected
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;red\x18
expect: bg=#ff0000
overrides: bg
gen: +1
step: feed \e]11;blue\x1a
expect: bg=#0000ff
cite: ADR 0022 D-CAN (OQ25 for queries): CAN and SUB end the OSC and dispatch what was collected; xterm ABORTS the string without dispatching, so xterm would keep the colour. Consequence of the parser, recorded as a decision
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### NK05_unterminated_name_does_nothing_yet

step: feed \e]11;red
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#101010 cursor=#ffcc00
overrides: none
gen: same
reply: none
cite: no terminator, no dispatch; the row ends with the OSC still open (each chunking sees the same)
flags: negative
